### 1) Run the AUB autopilot (module-level) and auto-select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for after it finishes:
- A new candidate evaluated against the same metrics as the current champion (`tuning_*`, `lockbox_*`).
- It should either:
  - promote a new champion (you’ll see an updated champion file / pointer), or
  - report no improvement and keep `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`.

If it fails or produces no outputs, capture the console log and any generated report paths.

### 2) Run the system autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What this usually does:
- Tries end-to-end/system configuration variants (often broader changes than a single module).
- Produces a comparison report and may generate a “best system candidate” recommendation depending on your tooling.

### 3) Generate the “next fix” report (actionable repair plan)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
This should produce:
- `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` with prioritized fixes based on observed failures/regressions, coverage gaps, or weak spots from recent runs.
